blocks.text: Walk into an optical shop on Marina and half the customers are collecting thin glasses for reading the chalkboard from the back of the class, while the other half want thicker lenses so they can thread a needle. Same pair of eyes, two opposite problems — and the optician solves each with a different kind of lens.

blocks.markdown:
A **lens** is a shaped piece of transparent material, usually glass or plastic, that refracts light so that a beam either comes together or spreads apart.

A **converging** (convex) lens is thicker in the middle than at the edges. Parallel rays that pass through it are bent **towards** the principal axis and meet at a **real** principal focus $F$ on the far side. Focal length $f$ is therefore **positive**.

A **diverging** (concave) lens is thinner in the middle. Parallel rays are bent **away** from the axis and appear to come from a **virtual** principal focus on the same side as the incoming light. Focal length $f$ is **negative**.

The **optical centre** $C$ is the midpoint of the lens. A ray through $C$ is undeviated. The **principal axis** is the line through $C$ and $F$.

blocks.title: Real-is-positive sign convention (WAEC)
blocks.text: Distances of real objects, real images and real foci are positive. Distances of virtual images and of the virtual focus of a diverging lens are negative. Object distance u is measured from the optical centre to the object and is positive for a real object. So f is positive for a converging lens and negative for a diverging lens. A negative v in your answer means the image is virtual.

blocks.title: Convex lens: finding the image
blocks.prompt: An object 2.0 cm high is placed 30 cm from a convex lens of focal length 10 cm. Find the position, nature and height of the image.

steps.text: Write the lens formula and make 1/v the subject. f is positive because the lens is converging.
Substitute f = +10 cm and u = 30 cm.
Invert. Positive v means the image is real, on the far side of the lens.
Find the magnification and then the image height.
The object is beyond 2F (2F = 20 cm), which matches the table: real, inverted and diminished.

blocks.answer: A real, inverted image 15 cm from the lens, 1.0 cm high

blocks.markdown:
### Power of a lens

The **power** $P$ of a lens measures how strongly it converges or diverges light:

$$P = \frac{1}{f}$$

Focal length **must** be in **metres**. The SI unit of power is the **dioptre** (D). A converging lens has **positive** power; a diverging lens has **negative** power. A lens of $f = 20\ \text{cm} = 0.20\ \text{m}$ has $P = +5.0\ \text{D}$.

### Spectacles

**Myopia** (short-sightedness) means a distant object is focused **in front of** the retina, so the far point is nearer than infinity. A **diverging** lens spreads the rays just enough for the eye to finish the focusing on the retina. Its power is negative.

**Hypermetropia** (long-sightedness) means a near object is focused **behind** the retina. A **converging** lens adds the extra bending the eye cannot supply. Its power is positive.

blocks.title: Power from focal length
blocks.prompt: A diverging lens used in a pair of spectacles has a focal length of 25 cm. Calculate its power.

steps.text: Convert the focal length to metres and attach the sign: a diverging lens has negative f.

blocks.answer: −4.0 D; the negative sign confirms a diverging (myopia) lens

items: Camera and projector lenses are convex; they form a real inverted image on the film or screen.
A simple magnifying glass is a convex lens with the object between F and the lens, giving a virtual, erect, magnified image.
The objective of a compound microscope and of a refracting telescope is a converging lens of short focal length.
Spectacles: diverging for myopia, converging for hypermetropia; the number stamped on the lens is its power in dioptres.

blocks.title: WAEC and JAMB tip
blocks.text: Convert f to metres before you calculate power — using centimetres gives an answer 100 times too large. Keep u, v and f in the same unit inside the lens formula. If v comes out negative, the image is virtual: do not then talk about catching it on a screen.

points: A converging (convex) lens is thicker in the middle and has a real, positive focus; a diverging (concave) lens is thinner in the middle and has a virtual, negative focus.
WAEC uses real-is-positive: 1/f = 1/u + 1/v and m = v/u = h_i/h_o, with f positive for a convex lens and negative for a concave lens.
A convex lens can form real or virtual images depending on object position; a concave lens always forms a virtual, erect, diminished image.
Power P = 1/f with f in metres; the unit is the dioptre (D). Converging lenses have +P, diverging lenses have −P.
Myopia is corrected with a diverging lens; hypermetropia is corrected with a converging lens.
